metrics.name: held_steady_voicing
metrics.threshold: steady pitch + unchanging spectrum >= 140 ms longer than reference

regions.explanation: At 10.77s, between “of” and “freedom—”, a 320 ms held vowel (“uh”/“um”) appears where the reference holds 0 ms, adding 593 ms at this word boundary. A held, unchanging vowel that maps to no word in the transcript is a filled pause; listeners hear it as hesitation, and judges penalise it under fluency. Fix: Replace the filler with silence - a clean pause sounds deliberate.

regions.text: beginning— signifying renewal as well as change. For
regions.explanation: From 16.07s to 21.44s (“beginning— signifying renewal as well as change. For”), 2 pause(s) at punctuation shrank from 1.04 s to 320 ms on average. Pauses at punctuation mark the end of an idea and give the audience time to absorb it; running through them merges separate thoughts into one stream. Fix: Hold a clear pause at each punctuation mark, about as long as the reference.

regions.text: fought are still at issue around
regions.explanation: From 57.76s to 60.72s (“fought are still at issue around”), loudness relative to the speaker's own level fell 8.8 dB below the reference, bottoming out 13.0 dB down; that is 1.8× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. The loudness falls away across the phrase, so its final words - often the payoff - drop toward the noise floor of the room. Fix: Support the breath through the end of the phrase; the last words need the same energy as the first.
